claim.value: Production causality requires confirmation and monitored rollout beyond boundary localization.
claim.scope: Limit on extending association under tested conditions to production causality; confirmation criteria are unspecified.

provenance.rationale: The span explicitly limits boundary localization to tested association and states the further confirmation and monitored-rollout requirement.

signal_basis.value: Repeated, evidence-based classifications of revision tail rates shrink the candidate transition interval, localizing an associated revision boundary without establishing a sole cause.
signal_basis.scope: Valid endpoints, comparable trials and a persistent single transition; classifications account for sampling uncertainty and repeated testing, and an unresolved interval remains when further classification is infeasible.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans supply the observations, classification safeguards, interval reduction, localization conditions and causal limitation.
This is a supported inferential limitation, not a conditional warrant requiring an unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: Boundary localization establishes association under tested conditions. It does not establish production causality, particularly because isolated replay may omit production interactions (P029). The claim faithfully states the mapping's requirement for further confirmation and monitored rollout; it does not claim those steps automatically prove causality.
uncertainty: Confirmation criteria are unspecified, so no conclusion about the sufficiency of any particular confirmation or rollout follows.
